# 31_parse_manuscript.sh - Markdown version of the manuscript

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`31_parse_manuscript.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

**Called from [bitbucket-pipelines.yml](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/replication-template/blob/master/bitbucket-pipelines.yml):**

:::

## Description

Downloads the PDF attachments of the Jira ticket into a scratch directory, converts the manuscript(s) with [manuscript_to_markdown.py](#help-manuscript_to_markdown), commits the result as `manuscript_parsed/` through `20_commit_code.sh` (no tag), and pushes it. The PDFs themselves are not committed here; `30_download_commit_jira_attachments.sh` does that.

The ingest pipelines may have pushed to the same branch in the meantime. `manuscript_parsed/` does not overlap anything they touch, so the push is retried up to five times after a `git pull --rebase`.

## Usage

```bash
. ./tools/resolve_jiraticket.sh
./automations/31_parse_manuscript.sh
```

### Environment Variables

- `jiraticket` - Required; set by `tools/resolve_jiraticket.sh`.
- `JIRA_USERNAME`, `JIRA_API_KEY` - Required for the attachment download.
- `BITBUCKET_BRANCH` - Branch to push to (default: the current branch).

With no manuscript among the attachments, the script reports that and exits 0 without committing.

See the [m-parse-manuscript pipeline](#pipeline-m-parse-manuscript), which runs it.
